dedupe_keys.name: medellin green corridors corredores verdes roads and waterways greened against urban heat

description: This case study describes Medellín's Green Corridors project, which turned the verges of 18 roads and 12 waterways into planted corridors to reduce the urban heat island in Colombia's second city. Oppla, the EU repository of nature-based solutions, publishes the case for the Alcaldía de Medellín. The project won the 2019 Ashden Award for Cooling by Nature, with support from the Kigali Cooling Efficiency Program in partnership with Sustainable Energy for All. The corridors shade cyclists and pedestrians, cool built areas and clean the air along busy roads, and the city's botanical garden trained 75 new gardeners, many displaced by armed conflict or from poor rural communities. Coverage is the City of Medellín in the Andes. Format and access: a case study web page. Licence: not stated; free. Caveats: the page gives no financing or measured temperature data for Medellín itself, citing general evidence from other cities, and dates it only to 2019. It illustrates street and riverside greening as heat adaptation of transport corridors. Related catalogue records are the Oppla repository and the Stuttgart ventilation corridors case.
